# Lawyer Assistant

> Lawyer Assistant is a free, open-source, local-first legal research desktop app.
> It reads your own legal documents (PDF, DOCX, OCR images, JSON, Markdown, plain text),
> lets you ask questions in plain English, and returns answers with inline citations
> pointing to the exact source passages. Everything runs on the user's machine — in
> local mode no question, document, or answer ever leaves it. Works fully offline with
> Ollama models, or connects to optional API providers (Claude, ChatGPT, Groq, Grok,
> DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Mistral, Gemini, OpenRouter, Together, OpenAI-compatible).

## What it does

- Cited answers: hybrid retrieval (BM25 keyword + dense vectors + reranker) grounds every
  answer in the user's documents; inline citations link claims to exact chunks.
- Compliance playbook scan: checks documents against configurable rules and flags risky
  language (e.g. missing required contract clauses), with persisted scan history.
- Visual pipeline editor: users can toggle dense/sparse/rerank/ingest/scan sub-nodes and
  rearrange retrieval flow without code.
- Local-first: BGE-M3 embeddings, ChromaDB vector store, BM25 index, BGE reranker, Ollama
  LLM — no cloud, no account, no telemetry.
- Any model: local Ollama models or optional API providers; API keys are stored locally
  and never shown after setup.
- Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux. Open source (MIT), source at
  https://github.com/haal-lab/Lawyer-Assistant.

## Key facts

- 100% private local mode; works offline; documents never uploaded to external servers.
- Hybrid search = BM25 + dense vectors fused and reranked.
- Ingests PDF, DOCX, OCR-readable images, JSON, Markdown, plain text.
- Backend: FastAPI on localhost port 8765; frontend: Vite + React; shell: Electron.
- Models: BGE-M3 (embeddings), BGE-Reranker-v2-M3, Ollama LLM; optional cloud APIs.

## Blog

Notes for lawyers on AI in legal work — practice notes, ethics, and the honest limits.

- [Blog hub](blog.html): all articles.
- [Disclosure Duties: Do You Have to Tell Clients You Use AI?](blog/ai-disclosure-duties.html): the five situations where disclosure is required, the state-by-state divide, and the courts' own disclosure regime.
- [ABA Formal Opinion 512 in Practice](blog/aba-formal-opinion-512-in-practice.html): the desk-level guide — competence, confidentiality, candor, supervision, and billing when you use AI.
- [AI and Attorney-Client Privilege](blog/ai-attorney-client-privilege.html): what happens when the machine sees the file — the doctrine, Heppner, and what makes the expectation of confidentiality reasonable.
- [AI vs. Westlaw and Lexis: What Actually Changed](blog/ai-vs-westlaw-lexis.html): the fair comparison — what AI adds, where the databases still win, the measured accuracy gap, and the hybrid workflow.
- [Verifying an AI's Case Citation in Five Minutes](blog/verifying-ai-case-citation.html): the workflow for checking AI-generated citations — existence, holding, treatment — with free tools and red flags.
- [How AI Legal Research Works Under the Hood](blog/how-ai-legal-research-works.html): the retrieval pipeline — keyword and semantic search, reranking, grounding — and why retrieval decides answer quality.
- [The Honest Limits of AI Contract Review](blog/honest-limits-ai-contract-review.html): where AI contract review fails in practice, and what still needs a human eye.
- [Building a Clause Playbook](blog/building-a-clause-playbook.html): turning your firm's judgment into AI-checkable contract review rules.
- [Force Majeure, Indemnification, and What AI Flags](blog/force-majeure-indemnification-ai-flags.html): the clauses lawyers fight over most, and what AI review flags in them.
- [How AI Reads a Contract](blog/how-ai-reads-a-contract.html): the contract-review pipeline explained — OCR, hybrid search, clause classification, playbook rules.
- [AI for Contract Review](blog/ai-contract-review-for-lawyers.html): what machines get right and what they miss.
- [How to Use AI for Legal Research Ethically](blog/how-to-use-ai-for-legal-research.html): ABA 512, competence, and a verification workflow.
- [Can You Trust an AI for Legal Research?](blog/can-you-trust-ai-legal-research.html): citations, grounding, and reliability.
- [Attorney–Client Privilege and AI](blog/attorney-client-privilege-and-ai.html): privilege, confidentiality, and local processing.
- [Will AI Replace Lawyers?](blog/will-ai-replace-lawyers.html): what the adoption data actually says.
- [Welcome to the Legal Desk](blog/welcome-to-the-legal-desk.html): what this blog is for.
